title: OpenAPI Contract Engineering
centralQuestion: What exactly does the API promise, and how can providers and consumers verify that promise?
responsibility: Define a precise, reviewable, executable HTTP API contract without confusing a description, a framework, and a running provider.
incomingBoundary: Basic programming ability, command-line familiarity, and no assumed OpenAPI experience.
outgoingBoundary: A frozen API 1.1 contract, operation ledger, schema fixtures, security decisions, workflow description, compatibility policy, and provider-neutral behavioral scenarios.
versionState: Public API 1.1; OpenAPI 3.1.2 executable baseline; OpenAPI 3.2.0 standards frontier; no durable database yet.

modules.title: HTTP and OpenAPI Foundations
modules.centralQuestion: How do raw HTTP exchanges become a public contract without confusing documentation with runtime behavior?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Establish health and project operations as raw messages, OpenAPI operations, and equivalent provider behavior.
learningOutcomes: Read requests and responses as protocol messages
Separate API behavior, OpenAPI description, implementation, and documentation rendering
Choose methods and status codes from HTTP semantics
Write a minimal valid OpenAPI description
Prove that the two reference providers expose the same public behavior

modules.title: Operations, Parameters, and Messages
modules.centralQuestion: How are parameters, request bodies, media types, status codes, and headers modeled without ambiguity?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Complete project and dataset messages, including pagination inputs, creation responses, and problem representations.
learningOutcomes: Model path, query, header, cookie, and body input deliberately
Use request bodies and media types correctly
Describe response codes, headers, and representations as a complete outcome
Choose stable operation identifiers
Validate examples against their schemas

modules.title: JSON Schema Contract Modeling
modules.centralQuestion: How do schemas reject invalid states while remaining usable for providers, clients, and future evolution?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Define precise project, dataset, run, artifact, and problem schemas with a shared valid/invalid fixture corpus.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish missing, null, empty, and default
Constrain objects, arrays, strings, and numbers precisely
Use composition as logic rather than inheritance
Design tagged unions and separate input/output models
Verify a shared corpus of valid and invalid instances

modules.title: References and Multi-Document Architecture
modules.centralQuestion: How can a multi-document contract remain understandable, relocatable, and deterministically buildable?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Split the contract into owned documents, resolve every reference offline, and produce deterministic bundles.
learningOutcomes: Resolve relative references from the correct document base
Use components where identity or reuse justifies them
Distinguish schema recursion from file-reference cycles
Bundle deterministically and work offline
Relocate the source tree without breaking resolution

modules.title: Production HTTP API Design
modules.centralQuestion: How should an HTTP API express asynchronous work, retries, conflicts, conditional updates, and machine-readable failures?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Add the analysis-run workflow, idempotency key, status resource, ETags, cancellation, and Problem Details.
learningOutcomes: Use `202 Accepted` with a status resource
Define idempotency-key behavior precisely
Use ETags and preconditions for optimistic concurrency
Design stable pagination and lifecycle-aware errors
Use RFC 9457 Problem Details as a public error vocabulary

modules.title: Contract-First and Code-First Runtimes
modules.centralQuestion: How do design-first and code-first descriptions relate, and how is semantic drift detected?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Map every operation to both providers and compare generated observations with the canonical contract.
learningOutcomes: Keep the canonical contract authoritative
Translate framework validation errors into the public problem model
Validate responses as well as requests
Classify generated-description drift
Preserve equivalent observable behavior across FastAPI and Fastify

modules.title: Mocks, Clients, and Contract Testing
modules.centralQuestion: How do mocks, generated clients, examples, property tests, and stateful tests provide different evidence?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Build the consumer and contract-test ladder against the mock and both real providers.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish syntax, semantic linting, conformance, and consumer tests
Develop consumers against a mock without mistaking examples for complete behavior
Generate and review clients in Python and TypeScript
Use generated and property-based tests to explore boundaries
Record tool capability limits instead of hiding them

modules.title: Security in the Public Contract
modules.centralQuestion: What can the public contract say about authentication and authorization, and what remains a runtime responsibility?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Describe API-key and OAuth-style schemes, scopes, anonymous overrides, and documented security failures.
learningOutcomes: Model API-key and bearer security schemes
Read AND/OR semantics in security requirements correctly
Use global security and operation overrides deliberately
Separate authentication, authorization, and ownership
Document security failures without leaking implementation details

modules.title: Evolution, Compatibility, and Audience Views
modules.centralQuestion: How can a published API evolve without silently breaking request writers or response readers?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Create compatible and rejected release candidates, compatibility gates, and public/partner audience views.
learningOutcomes: Analyze compatibility in the correct message direction
Treat requiredness, enums, media types, statuses, and operation IDs as consumer commitments
Design deprecation and major-version migration
Apply Overlay documents deterministically
Block incompatible minor releases in CI

modules.title: OpenAPI 3.2, Streaming, Webhooks, and Workflows
modules.centralQuestion: How do current OpenAPI features express streaming, webhooks, links, query methods, and multi-step workflows?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the OpenAPI 3.2 frontier, streaming and webhook contracts, links, and an Arazzo workflow.
learningOutcomes: Maintain a broadly executable OpenAPI 3.1 baseline
Use OpenAPI 3.2 features where they add real meaning
Model SSE and JSON Lines streams
Connect operations with links, callbacks, webhooks, and runtime expressions
Describe a multi-step outcome with Arazzo and record tool support honestly
